skill.name: antislop-ui
skill.description: Guides interface reviews and improvements across brand identity, layout, components, motion, and page performance, alongside the antislop core.
skill.summary: Replace generic interface patterns with purposeful design choices, working controls, honest content, and evidence-based performance improvements.
skill.author: miqdadbadjuber

content.value_statement: Generic interface patterns can obscure product identity, real workflows, and usability problems. This skill guides focused design reviews and implementation changes using explicit purpose, honest content, and measured performance evidence.
actual_capabilities: Identify generic palette, typography, layout, decoration, and motion choices and suggest purpose-based alternatives.
Review navigation and controls for real destinations, working behavior, and clear unfinished states.
Assess dashboard hierarchy, table columns, charts, and metrics against the decisions users need to make.
Recommend honest placeholders and useful empty, loading, and error states instead of fabricated activity or data.
Guide evidence-based LCP, INP, and CLS diagnosis while separating lab observations from field measurements.
Provide optional page-baseline checks for semantic HTML, HTTPS, client-side secrets, third-party integrity, and permission timing.
limitations: The companion antislop core is referenced but is not included in this skill package.
Runtime performance claims require external measurement tools, a runnable page, or supplied field data.
The package provides written guidance and examples, not an executable scanner or automated test suite.
Its checklists do not replace comprehensive accessibility testing, security auditing, or product-specific design judgment.

use_cases.title: Refine an existing interface
use_cases.description: Review colors, typography, spacing, and decoration against product identity, then propose specific changes with clear reasons.

use_cases.title: Improve an operational dashboard
use_cases.description: Align tables, charts, controls, and interface states with the next decision users need to make.

use_cases.title: Prepare a page for release
use_cases.description: Review media sizing, image priority, script loading, and page-baseline checks while separating observed defects from unmeasured performance hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Review visual defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface for generic visual patterns. List five specific improvements based on the supplied brand identity and explain the purpose of each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain a focused first review.

prompt_templates.title: Repair controls and states
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this page for dead navigation, nonfunctional controls, and unclear empty, loading, or error states. Implement focused fixes and identify unresolved dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve interaction quality in an existing page.

prompt_templates.title: Reorganize a dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: The primary user decision is [decision]. Review this dashboard against that decision. Rework hierarchy, columns, charts, and states without inventing metrics or activity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: align an operational interface with its workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose measured performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supplied field data and browser trace to diagnose [metric] on [page]. Separate field and lab evidence, implement targeted fixes, and repeat equivalent measurements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate a measured Core Web Vitals problem.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard containing invented statistics, repeated activity entries, and a generic table.
output: Remove unsupported statistics and fabricated activity, or label prototype values visibly as placeholders.
Place the field that determines the next user action early in the table.
Replace the empty feed with a clear explanation and a relevant first action.

output_examples.input: Review source showing an unsized hero image, lazy loading above the fold, and synchronous third-party scripts.
output: Reserve media dimensions to reduce layout-shift risk.
Make the hero image discoverable in the initial HTML and prioritize its loading.
LCP, INP, and CLS remain unmeasured until runtime evidence is available.

best_practices: Provide the companion core, brand guidance, and the primary user decision before requesting substantial interface changes.
Use real data or clearly labeled placeholders, and verify every visible control has meaningful behavior.
Test relevant breakpoints, themes, states, and keyboard interactions; report performance numbers only when measured.
anti_patterns: Apply blanket visual bans without considering brand identity, content, or user needs.
Invent customer logos, metrics, activity entries, or performance results to make an interface appear complete.
Treat a polished screenshot as proof that navigation, accessibility, and runtime behavior work.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers interface color, layout, components, decoration, motion, workflow clarity, performance review, and optional page-baseline checks.

faq.question: Does it require the antislop core?
faq.answer: The instructions explicitly pair it with the antislop core. That companion document is not included in this package.

faq.question: Can it review dashboards as well as websites?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes dashboard hierarchy, metrics, charts, table columns, data placeholders, and interface states alongside website design patterns.

faq.question: Does it automatically measure Core Web Vitals?
faq.answer: No. It provides measurement guidance and interpretation references. Actual results require runtime tools or supplied field data.

faq.question: Are gradients, grids, and common fonts always forbidden?
faq.answer: No. The guidance asks for choices justified by content, brand identity, and purpose instead of automatic use of familiar defaults.

faq.question: Does the page-baseline checklist replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It covers selected web security defaults, not comprehensive vulnerability testing or application-specific security review.
